killed_candidate.name: Thermoelectric CSF Temperature Gradient Harvester
killed_candidate.kill_reason: Physics attack: 2°C gradient produces 0.16 nW (Seebeck calculation). Need >1 μW. Insufficient by 6000x.
killed_candidate.cemetery_entry: CE-029 — thermoelectric CSF harvesting insufficient. 2°C gradient produces 0.16 nW. Future thermal harvesting candidates must calculate Seebeck power before admission.
killed_candidate.reusable_negative_knowledge: Thermoelectric harvesting from CSF temperature gradient is infeasible. 2°C core-subcutaneous gradient × 200 μV/K Seebeck × typical resistance = sub-nW. Unlike P-15 (cardiac motion, 10 μW) or P-16 (NIR, ~1050 μW), thermal gradient in the body is too small for useful power.

P-24.name: Gravity-Compensating Hydraulic Damper
P-24.mechanism: Passive hydraulic damper that increases flow resistance proportionally to postural pressure changes
P-24.why_promoted: Survived all 6 attacks. Addresses overdrainage (15% of failures). Mechanism is purely mechanical (no electronics, no biology). Distinct from existing portfolio. Novel approach: proportional damping vs fixed-threshold anti-siphon devices.
P-24.next_action: Build computational model: damper response curve vs pressure differential. Compare to anti-siphon device.

P-25.name: Self-Referencing Piezoresistive Pressure Sensor with Zero-Drift Compensation
P-25.mechanism: Dual-element piezoresistive sensor with real-time zero-drift compensation through differential measurement
P-25.why_promoted: Survived all 6 attacks. Addresses sensor drift (3% of failures, $50K each — highest cost per event). Mechanism is proven physics (differential measurement is standard in sensor engineering). Distinct from existing portfolio. Novel application: chronic implantable CSF pressure sensing.
P-25.next_action: Build computational model: dual-element sensor drift model, compare to single-element over 30-day thermal cycling.
